title: Sparse exemplar surgery — scratchpad
content:
Goal: explore a lightweight technique I call 'sparse exemplar surgery' — surgical replacement/curation of 2–5 few-shot exemplars at inference time to reduce hallucination and label-confusion without re-finetuning.

Context: too many templates assume static few-shot sets. For long-tail tasks (taxonomy assignment, instruction-following with strict formatting) models degrade when exemplars are noisy or internally inconsistent. Idea: keep a digital 'suture kit' of candidate exemplars and a tiny policy that picks which exemplars to inject per request based on simple heuristics.

Hypotheses: 
- H1: Replacing 1 exemplar (the one with highest lexical overlap to prompt but mismatched label) reduces class-confusion by >= 15% in prompting budgets < 200 tokens.
- H2: Rotating exemplars based on exemplar-age + failure-rate prevents drift for streaming workloads.

Setup / quick recipe: 
- Base model: open-llama-13b-v2-like (dev sim). Proxy: hosted API v1 call with temperature 0.0 -> 0.6 for robustness sweep.
- Candidate exemplar pool: 24 curated examples per task (balanced across labels). Each exemplar has metadata: created_at, last_used, fail_count, lexical_signature (top 10 tokens), canonical_label.
- Selector heuristics (cheap, run client-side):
  * overlap_penalty: if exemplar shares > 60% important tokens with prompt and canonical_label != expected_label_hint -> mark for replacement.
  * recency_boost: prefer exemplars last_used > 3 days ago for rotation (avoids repeating same examples).
  * fail_score: exemplar.fail_count > threshold -> deprioritize.
- Replacement policy: pick a replacement exemplar with same label but lower overlap and lower fail_count. If none available, fallback to synthetic exemplar derived by template + slot-fill.

Prompt scaffolding (template used in experiments):
  "You are an assistant that maps a short product description to one of {A,B,C}. Follow exact output format: LABEL:<one-letter>.

  Examples:
  {exemplar_block}

  Now label: 
  Input: 
  {user_input}
  Output:"

Exemplar_block generation: 2–4 exemplars, each as "Description -> LABEL:X" lines.

Experiment log (choppy notes):
- run 2025-11-13: 4-shot baseline (static exemplars) on 1k eval set -> acc 72.4% (T=0.0).
- apply sparse surgery (replace 1 exemplar by overlap_penalty) -> acc 78.1% (+5.7%). big wins on cases where prompt mentions competing entity names.
- counterexample: prompt_length > 120 tokens -> effect size smaller (~+1.5%). hypothesis: longer context dilutes exemplar signal.
- run 2025-11-17: rotation enabled (age + fail_count), 2-week simulated stream -> cumulative acc drift reduced from -6% to -1.2% vs baseline.

Failure categories observed: 
1) label collapse: model repeats label from last exemplar regardless of input (happens when exemplars phrasing is highly similar). Fix tried: diversify surface forms; partial improvement.
2) anchoring to number tokens: exemplars containing counts ("3 features") cause model to prioritize numeric cues. Patch: mask counts in exemplars where irrelevant.
3) synthetic exemplar poisoning: fallback synthesis occasionally produces ambiguous label assignments -> add conservative filter (reject if softmax margin < 0.25).

Quick qualitative examples (annotated):
- prompt: "Lightweight auth for mobile SDK, requires offline-first"
  baseline exemplars -> LABEL:B (incorrect)
  after replacement -> LABEL:C (correct) — replaced exemplar had strong lexical overlap on "mobile" but labeled different category.

- prompt: "Billing reconciliation for high-volume merchants"
  baseline -> LABEL:A (low confidence)
  surgery -> LABEL:A (higher confidence) — replaced noisy exemplar mentioning "monthly invoices" which confused micro vs macro flows.

Open questions / TODOs: 
- Q1: Should the selector consider model logits as part of feedback loop? cheap proxy: run a 1-token probe and measure cross-entropy. Tradeoff: cost vs signal.
- Q2: How many exemplars is the knee? current tests at 1–4; try 0,1,2,4,8 in next sweep.
- Q3: Interaction with function-calling / structured output: need to ensure surgery doesn't break required fields. Add unit tests.
- TODO: push a small PoC to GH branch "sparse-exemplar-poc". Patch script that reads /writes exemplar metadata as jsonl.
- TODO: add CI check: synthetic exemplar generation must pass margin filter.

Notes-to-self: 
- keep temperature low for deterministic label checks (0.0–0.2); use 0.4 for human-like paraphrase tasks.
- instrument latency impact: selector should run <5ms on client; otherwise move to edge.
- think about privacy: exemplar pool per-tenant vs global. default per-tenant but fallback safe-public exemplars.

Links & refs: 
- inspiration: few papers on exemplar selection & retrieval-augmented prompts (add proper citations later).
- internal: GH:repo/prompt-bank#142 has the exemplar pool export.

Scratchy checklist before next sync with Ravi / Sofia: 
- [ ] run full sweep with temperature grid and 0/1/2 replacement budgets (deadline 2025-11-27)
- [ ] add synthetic exemplar margin filter + unit tests (deadline 2025-11-25)
- [ ] instrument per-request selector time + cost (deadline 2025-11-24)
- [ ] write short one-pager summarizing results for weekly research sync

Random personal footnote: this feels useful for Dedicated customers who want small client-side heuristics to squeeze production quality without changing server-side model artifacts. Keep it simple.

End of scratchpad.
